newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE, RUSSIA EXPLORE DEFENCE COOPERATION.
newsitem.headline: GREECE, RUSSIA EXPLORE DEFENCE COOPERATION.

text.p: Greece signed on Friday a cooperation protocol with Russia to explore the possibility of joint production and supply of defence material, Deputy Defence Minister Dimitris Apostolakis said.
"Today's agreement is of a more general nature and nothing has yet been finalised," Apostolakis told a news conference after meeting with a Russian defence ministry delegation visiting Greece.

Greece has announced a massive armaments programme to boost its defence capability. It intends to spend $17 billion by the year 2007 to purchase tanks, submarines, air defence systems, AWAX flying radars, ships.
Ministry officials had said that most of the supplies would come from the U.S. and other European countries.

Apostolakis said Russia had a well-developed industry in missiles and anti-aircraft systems. A squadron of Russian aircraft could take part in a joint exercise with Greece's airforce this Spring, he added.
Asked to comment on the possibility of Russia supplying Greece with aircraft, he said that this entailed a long and complex process which had not yet reached the level of talks.
"Russian aircraft are good but Greece's system of maintenance and spare parts is American and the shift to another system is a long process," he said.
Apostolakis acknowledged that "displeasure" had been expressed at a diplomatic level as Greece would be the first NATO member to purchase Russian weapon systems.
He clarified, however that the pressure being exerted was not of the type "don't buy from them" but rather "buy from us".

Cyprus, which has a joint defence pact with Greece, announced recently it was buying Russian anti-aircraft missile systems, prompting strong reaction from Turkey and Western allies concerned over the arms buildup on the Mediterranean island.
